meta.description: Trim PCR primers from aligned reads in amplicon-panel BAMs using samtools ampliconclip. Use when processing SARS-CoV-2 ARTIC, hereditary cancer panels, ctDNA hot-spot panels, or any amplicon assay where primer-derived bases would falsely confirm reference at primer footprints.
meta.environment: WSL science env alignment-files: samtools 1.24, pysam 0.24.1, iVar 1.4.4, fgbio 4.1.1 (af-fgbio2); real data: nf-core ARTIC v5.3.2 nanopore BAM + primer BED, MN908947.3 FASTA, Illumina SARS-CoV-2 PE BAM; synthetic: run/data/ (labelled SYNTHETIC)

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated citations or numbers in outputs; the Grubaugh 2019 Genome Biol 20:8 (iVar) citation and the artic minion align_trim statement are correct

practice_boundaries.detail: Processing-tool Skill with no diagnostic or prescriptive content; hereditary-cancer and ctDNA panels are mentioned only as assay types

methodological_ground.detail: Core method (post-alignment primer soft-clip, then mate and MD/NM repair; never markdup amplicon BAMs) is sound and verified against planted truth; the strand/both-ends misstatements are tool-behaviour errors, recorded as P1, not a principled methodological fallacy

code_usability.detail: Every snippet and the shipped example ran from a copy on samtools 1.24 and produced asserted correct output on valid inputs (5/5 inputs executed); the 5-column BED example fails only with --strand and is recorded as P1

functional_suitability.note: Core clip/fixmate/calmd workflow verified correct on real and synthetic data; but the both-ends/strand override claim, the strand-bias diagnosis and the fgbio ClipBam row are wrong, the BED example fails with --strand, and ARTIC nanopore reads need --both-ends without saying so

reliability.note: Shipped example exits 0 on a contig mismatch and on a wrong calmd reference (stderr to /dev/null); no verification of clip counts or MD presence; input untouched and temp dir cleaned

performance_context.note: 160-line SKILL.md with usage-guide.md repeating decision points and tips; workflow is linear (collate variant in the example is efficient)

agent_usability.note: Clear stepwise workflow but inconsistent between sections (strand col 5 vs col 6, --strand default vs example using --both-ends, override claim vs behaviour); no success assertion or expected output

human_usability.note: Natural trigger phrasing; brittle to the Skill's own BED format and silent on mismatched inputs

security.note: No credentials; variables quoted; mktemp/trap cleanup; no input checks on paths or contig names

maintainability.note: Three files with a clear split; one example, no test data or expected output, no version-specific notes for ampliconclip options

agent_specific.note: Precise trigger; deterministic and rerunnable; related-skill pointers exist (all targets found) but SKILL.md and usage-guide.md duplicate content; stop condition for markdup present, few others

inputs.label: Real ARTIC v5.3.2 nanopore BAM: Skill's basic workflow verbatim
inputs.note: Executed on real data. Every clip is correct against a BED-derived oracle and calmd MD/NM are exact, but the recommended --strand leaves the 3' primer footprint in 97.5% of full-length reads and the Skill has no check that says so.

assertions.text: Every clipped forward read starts exactly at a '+' primer end and every clipped reverse read ends at a '-' primer start (BED-derived oracle)
assertions.note: 2353/2353 forward and 2471/2471 reverse clipped reads match; 0 bad

assertions.text: calmd MD and NM equal an independent recomputation from reference, CIGAR and SEQ
assertions.note: 0 MD and 0 NM mismatches over 4916 reads; raw ampliconclip output had removed NM and MD on all 4916

assertions.text: Final BAM is coordinate-sorted, indexed and keeps every record
assertions.note: sort -n | fixmate -m | sort then calmd; index OK; 4916 in, 4916 out

assertions.text: No primer-derived bases remain at either end of the read after the Skill's recommended strand-aware run
assertions.note: 97.5% (4793/4916) of reads still have the 3' end inside an opposite-strand primer footprint under --strand; 0% under --both-ends

assertions.text: Result agrees with an independent tool (iVar trim) on the same reads
assertions.note: --strand vs iVar: 114/4824 identical (name,flag,pos,cigar); --both-ends vs iVar: 4674/4909 (95%)

inputs.execution_note: run/i1_real_artic.sh, i1_check.py, i1b_ivar_compare.sh, i1c_modes.sh, i1d_residual.py; samtools 1.24, pysam 0.24.1, iVar 1.4.4.

inputs.label: Synthetic paired-end panel through the shipped example script, planted SNP under a primer
inputs.note: Executed from a copy. 800/800 reads match planted truth in every mode, TLEN/MPOS/MC/ms repaired, planted SNP VAF 0.50 to 1.00, markdup marks 89% of reads.

assertions.text: Clipped read boundaries equal the planted primer boundaries in default, --strand, --both-ends, --both-ends --strand, --hard-clip and the shipped example
assertions.note: 800/800 in all six runs (jittered 5' starts inside the 5-base tolerance included)

assertions.text: Mate fields repaired after clipping (MPOS, TLEN, MC, ms)
assertions.note: 0 bad MPOS, 0 bad TLEN, MC equals mate CIGAR, ms present, for every mode

assertions.text: calmd MD/NM equal independent recomputation, including hard-clipped reads
assertions.note: 0 mismatches in all six outputs

assertions.text: Planted variant under a primer is recovered after clipping
assertions.note: pos310 T:100/C:100 before, T:100 after; pos335 A:100/G:100 before, G:100 after

assertions.text: Skill's claim that markdup on an amplicon BAM marks essentially every read is reproduced
assertions.note: 710/800 (88.8%) marked duplicate on 5'-jittered synthetic pairs

inputs.execution_note: run/make_synth.py (SYNTHETIC data), i2_synth.sh, i2_check.py; shipped examples/ampliconclip_workflow.sh run from run/out/i2/skillcopy.

inputs.label: --strand / --both-ends semantics and the Skill's own BED format (synthetic reads)
inputs.note: Executed. The 'both-ends overrides strand' claim is contradicted by behaviour, the strand-bias diagnosis is inverted, and the Skill's 5-column BED example makes --strand fail.

assertions.text: Without --strand a reverse read whose 5' end sits in a '+' primer is clipped (off-strand over-clipping, as the Skill states)
assertions.note: c1: default 251:50M10S, --strand 251:60M

assertions.text: A '#' comment line at the top of the BED (as in the Skill's example) is accepted
assertions.note: no parse error; run completes

assertions.text: --both-ends with --strand gives the same result as --both-ends alone (Skill: '--both-ends overrides --strand')
assertions.note: c4 50M30S vs 75M5S, c5 50M15S vs 65M, c7 20S50M vs 70M; real ARTIC data 4830 vs 4817 forward-clipped reads. The man page says 'ignored'; the 1.24 binary does not ignore it

assertions.text: The Skill's BED example (5 columns, strand in column 5) works with --strand
assertions.note: samtools ampliconclip --strand: 'Parsed 5 columns, but need at least 6', exit 1; the prose says column 6 while the example puts the strand in column 5

assertions.text: 'Variant calls with strand bias at every amplicon end | Forgot --strand' is a consistent diagnosis
assertions.note: forgetting --strand only adds off-strand clipping (c1); real data: 4834 clipped without vs 4824 with, so it cannot leave primer bases on one strand

inputs.execution_note: run/i3_strand_cases.py + i3_strand_cases.sh: 8 planted single-read geometries x 4 flag sets, plus the 5-column BED.

inputs.label: Hard-clip archive copy, tool alternatives (iVar, fgbio ClipBam) and IUPAC consensus
inputs.note: Executed. Hard-clip, iVar and consensus claims verified against planted truth; fgbio ClipBam has no primer input at all and clips a fixed length, so it is not the BED-driven alternative the table implies.

assertions.text: --hard-clip removes the primer bases from SEQ (irreversible) and downstream repair still works
assertions.note: 800/800 H-CIGAR reads, mean SEQ length 94.9 to 70.3, boundaries match truth, calmd MD/NM exact

assertions.text: 'samtools consensus --config hiseq --ambig' after clipping returns the planted alleles; before clipping it emits IUPAC codes
assertions.note: unclipped Y at 310 and R at 335; clipped T and G (planted ALT)

assertions.text: iVar trim gives the same boundaries as samtools ampliconclip on the same primer BED
assertions.note: 800/800 exactly match planted truth for both tools

assertions.text: fgbio ClipBam can consume a primer BED as the Tool Selection table implies
assertions.note: 0 of 101 help lines mention bed/primer/amplicon; the closest use (fixed 25-base 5' clip) matched truth for 632/800 (79%)

assertions.text: Soft clip keeps the trimmed bases in SEQ so the clip is reversible
assertions.note: soft-clipped output: 800/800 reads byte-identical SEQ to the original, S ops in CIGAR (i4b_softseq.sh); ampliconclip --original also exists but is not mentioned

inputs.execution_note: run/i4_tools.sh, i4_check.py (SYNTHETIC data); fgbio 4.1.1 side env, iVar 1.4.4, samtools consensus 1.24.

inputs.note: Executed. With MT192765.1 reads and the MN908947.3 ARTIC BED the example exits 0 with 0 reads clipped; with the wrong FASTA calmd fails silently (stderr sent to /dev/null), exit 0, and the output BAM carries no MD tags.

assertions.note: F1: example exit 0, 'Clipped BAM:' printed, TOTAL CLIPPED: 0, 200 records unchanged; nothing in the Skill says to compare contig names or check TOTAL CLIPPED

assertions.note: F2: exit 0, f2.bam + .bai written; calmd's '[bam_fillmd] fail to find sequence' is discarded by 2>/dev/null; output has 0 MD tags on 4916 reads

assertions.note: F2 output: 0 MD, 7 NM of 4916

assertions.text: Example is safe on inputs: temp dir, quoted variables, input untouched, temp cleaned
assertions.note: mktemp -d + trap cleanup, all variables quoted; identical record md5 across THREADS=4/1/4 runs

assertions.text: ampliconclip's own statistics reveal the no-op
assertions.note: raw run prints 'TOTAL CLIPPED: 0' on stderr, but the example does not test it

key_strengths: The core recipe (ampliconclip, sort -n | fixmate -m | sort, calmd -b, index) is correct: 4824/4824 real clips and 800/800 synthetic clips match BED-derived truth, TLEN/MPOS/MC/ms and MD/NM are exact afterwards

Verified 'why' claims: a planted SNP under a primer goes from VAF 0.50 to 1.00 after clipping, IUPAC codes disappear in samtools consensus --config hiseq --ambig, and markdup marks 89% of amplicon reads
Soft-clip default, hard-clip irreversibility, 0-based half-open BED, since-1.11 and the artic minion / iVar attribution notes are all accurate; every file the Skill points at exists
Deterministic and safe: identical record md5 across three runs and thread counts, quoted variables, mktemp workdir with trap cleanup, input never modified

recommendations.title: Shipped example succeeds silently on mismatched inputs
recommendations.problem: With a BAM on MT192765.1 and an MN908947.3 primer BED the example exits 0 and reports 'Clipped BAM' with TOTAL CLIPPED: 0; with the wrong reference FASTA calmd fails, its stderr goes to /dev/null, and the output BAM has no MD tags at exit 0.
recommendations.root_cause: The example does no input checks and discards calmd's stderr; SKILL.md has no verification step.
recommendations.fix: In ampliconclip_workflow.sh compare BAM @SQ names with BED column 1 and the FASTA .fai and stop on no overlap, drop 2>/dev/null on calmd, and assert TOTAL CLIPPED > 0 and MD present (samtools view -c ... | grep -c MD:Z) before printing success. Add a 'Verify' step to SKILL.md.

recommendations.title: '--both-ends overrides --strand' and the strand-bias diagnosis are wrong
recommendations.problem: On samtools 1.24 --both-ends --strand differs from --both-ends alone (synthetic c4, c5, c7; real ARTIC 4830 vs 4817 forward-clipped reads). The Common Errors row says forgetting --strand causes strand bias at every amplicon end, but forgetting it only adds off-strand clipping.
recommendations.root_cause: The override statement was copied from the samtools man page without being tested, and the error row has cause and remedy inverted.
recommendations.fix: State that --strand restricts which primers (by BED strand) can clip each read end, also with --both-ends, and give the tested outcomes. Rewrite the row: primer bases surviving at every amplicon end means the wrong or missing ampliconclip, tolerance too small, or 3' primers not clipped (--both-ends).

recommendations.title: ARTIC/long-read default (--strand) leaves the 3' primer in nearly all reads
recommendations.problem: On the real ARTIC v5.3.2 nanopore BAM the recommended strand-aware run leaves 97.5% of reads with the 3' end inside a primer footprint (0% with --both-ends) and agrees with iVar on only 114 of 4824 reads (4674/4909 with --both-ends).
recommendations.root_cause: The <300 bp rule for --both-ends ignores read length; full-length long reads carry both primers regardless of amplicon size.
recommendations.fix: Make the --both-ends rule depend on whether reads span the whole amplicon (nanopore, long reads, read length >= amplicon), say ARTIC nanopore needs it, and add a check that counts reads with a 3' end still inside a primer.

recommendations.title: Primer BED example is 5-column but --strand needs column 6
recommendations.problem: The example puts the strand in column 5 (chr1 100 125 primer_1_F +); samtools ampliconclip --strand rejects it: 'Parsed 5 columns, but need at least 6', exit 1. The prose next to it says column 6.
recommendations.root_cause: Illustrative BED written without running it.
recommendations.fix: Replace with a real 6-column example (chrom, start, end, name, score, strand) and note that 7-column ARTIC BEDs are accepted.

recommendations.title: fgbio ClipBam presented as a primer-trimming alternative
recommendations.problem: fgbio 4.1.1 ClipBam has no BED, primer or amplicon option; it clips a fixed number of bases (matched planted truth on 79% of reads with a fixed 25-base clip) or overlapping mates.
recommendations.root_cause: Tool listed by association with mate-aware clipping, not checked against its options.
recommendations.fix: Remove ClipBam from the primer-trimming alternatives or describe it as fixed-length/overlap clipping for a different job; replace with a tool that does take a primer file.

recommendations.title: Raw ampliconclip output is unsorted and unclipped reads are invisible
recommendations.problem: The Quick Reference command writes a BAM with SO:unknown that samtools index rejects ('Unsorted positions'); 92 reads (1.9%) with no matching primer pass through unclipped without mention, and --clipped, --tolerance, --fail, --primer-counts and --original are not covered. MD and NM are deleted by default, not stale.
recommendations.root_cause: Only the flags used in the workflow are documented; the man page caveats were not carried over.
recommendations.fix: Say the output must be re-sorted before indexing, document the unclipped-read count and --clipped/--tolerance/--primer-counts, and change 'invalidated' to 'removed by default (--keep-tag keeps them)'.

recommendations.title: Duplicated content and one invalid pointer
recommendations.problem: usage-guide.md repeats SKILL.md's decision points and tips nearly verbatim; the pileup-generation pointer '-aa -A -d 600000 -B' is valid for samtools mpileup but bcftools mpileup rejects '-aa' ('Could not parse tag a').
recommendations.root_cause: Documents drifted apart and the flags were not run with both tools.
recommendations.fix: Keep decision points in one file and name the tool in the pointer.
